name: Quote
description: Text quoted from another source, marked up as <blockquote> with an optional attribution. Its pull quote variant repeats a line from the page in large type for emphasis.
summary: Quoted text with an optional attribution
researchNote: A pull quote repeats text already on the page, so hide the duplicate from screen readers

elements.name: Quote text
elements.description: The quoted words, as one or more paragraphs

elements.name: Attribution
elements.description: Who said it, in <figcaption>; the title of the work goes in <cite>

elements.name: Quote mark
elements.description: Decorative quotation mark, hidden from screen readers

variants.caption: Block quote — indented with a rule at the start
Pull quote — large text beside the body
Centered — large text with a quote mark

usageNotes: Use <blockquote> only for quoted text, never just to indent. For a short quote inside a sentence, use <q>.
Put the attribution in a <figcaption> inside a <figure>, outside the <blockquote>. <cite> marks the title of a work, not the person's name.
A pull quote repeats text already on the page, so hide the duplicate from screen readers with aria-hidden="true" and don't mark it up as a <blockquote>.
Add decorative quotation marks with CSS or an aria-hidden graphic so they aren't read aloud.
For a customer quote with a name, photo and role, use Testimonial.
